To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients with atherosclerotic diseases had a higher antioxidant capacity than healthy individuals.

the plasma of patients with atherosclerotic lesions had a lower peroxide-depend chemoluminescence than healthy individuals, which is explained by the increased activity of the plasma antioxidant system in the patients.

the antioxidant state of patients with atherosclerotic diseases was evaluated by peroxide-dependant chemiluminesence and inhibition of azoinitiated chemiluminesce and hydrogen peroxide hemoglobin luminol chemiluminscence system and that the flash amplitude of peroxid dependent chemiluminescense in plasma of patients with atheroscierosis was 32% lower than in the controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the antioxidant state in patients with atheromatous diseases.
the evaluation of antioxidant activity of the blood in patients with coronary heart and obliterating athero-sclerosis.
the development of new methods of antioxidant therapy for the treatment of patients with cardiovascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidant status of atherosclerosis patients is higher than that of healthy individuals.
atherosclerosis is not a disease of cholesterol, but rather a disease of free radicals.

the results obtained by chemiluminescent analysis are consistent with the hypothesis that the oxidative stress is involved in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and that the oxidative stress may be an important factor in the development of atherosclerosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decrease in peroxidase-dependent chemiluminecence of blood plasma in patients with atherogenesis is due to an increase in the antioxidant activity of the plasma.
the antioxidant activity of plasma in atherosclerosis is increased and this is due to the activation of antioxidant enzymes.
atherosclerosis is associated with the decrease in peroxidative processes, and this decrease is due to increased activity of endogenous antioxidant systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemiluminescent assay can be used for monitoring the antioxidant state of patients with atherosclerotic diseases.
the chemiluminescent methods of antioxidant state evaluation in patients with atherogenic pathology are promising for the diagnosis and monitoring of the disease.

the antioxidant system of patients with atheroscleroses is activated and that the increase in antioxidant activity is most pronounced in patients suffering from coronary heart disease and obliterating atheriosclerosis of lower extremeties.
